title: Monocyte Transmigration Study Across Human Liver Endothelial Cells Under Shear Flow
author: Wilkinson, Bannister, et al.
materials:
Timing: 1 h
1.Enzyme digestion stock (Collagenase I)∗.a.Sterile PBS was used to reconstitute Collagenase I to a working concentration of 10 mg/mL.
Note: ∗Aliquots of this can be made in advance and stored at −20°C for up to 1 year to reduce the time spent preparing reagents when performing this protocol.
2.Liver endothelial cell medium.a.Described in key resources table.3.Percoll dilutions.a.Prepare a working solution of stock Percoll with 99 mL Percoll and 11 mL 10x PBS.b.Prepare a 33% Percoll dilution of 33 mL Percoll and 67 mL 1x PBS.c.Prepare a 77% Percoll dilution of 77 mL Percoll and 23 mL 1x PBS.
Note: Percoll stock and dilutions can be stored at 2°C–8°C for up to 6 months.
4.Reconstitute Fixable Viability Stain 620 LIVE DEAD Stain.a.Add 230 μL fresh cell culture-grade Dimethyl Sulfoxide (DMSO) and vortex.
Note: Reconstituted LIVE DEAD Stain can be stored at −20°C for up to 1 year.
5.Prepare MACS Buffer.a.Described in key resources table.

Timing: 0.5 h
6.Switch on Class II Microbiological Safety Cabinet (MSC).7.Preheat orbital shaker (37°C).8.Switch on BD Bioscience LSRFortessa X-20.a.The laser configuration used for this protocol is as follows: 488 nm Blue, 640 nm Red, 405 nm Violet, 561 nm Yellow/Green, 355 nm Ultra Violet.
Note: This is a suggested flow cytometer and configuration, the following protocol can be run on various cytometers and configurations depending on instrumentation and reagent availability.
Note: Antibody concentrations used were determined by single color titration and with appropriate compensation applied. Positive staining was determined based on a matched isotype control.
9.Coat T25 and T75 tissue culture flasks with rat tail collagen. (refer to section materials and equipment for preparation).

The following protocol describes the specific steps for the isolation of primary liver endothelial cells from explanted and rejected donor human liver tissues. The major steps are illustrated in Figure 1. For optimal results when isolating liver endothelial cells, human liver tissue samples should be placed in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagles Medium (DMEM) and stored at 4°C until processed.Note: Whilst some phenotypic changes will inevitably occur in vitro, we have previously demonstrated that primary human liver endothelial cells isolated using our protocol still maintain important phenotypic features, such as their capacity for rapid endocytosis via scavenger receptors and their unique junctional profile.2 Furthermore, they are phenotypically distinct from more conventional vascular endothelia, such as human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs).2 Liver endothelial cells were used up to passage 5.CRITICAL: To maintain aseptic conditions, the following protocol needs to be carried out in a Class II Biological Safety Cabinet.1.Digestion of liver tissue to a single cell suspension.a.Mechanically chop ∼75 g of human liver tissue with sterile scalpels in a 150 × 20 mm petri dish, until you reach the consistency of a course paste (Figure 1Aii).Note: Before chopping the liver, try to excise any highly vascular regions which will be rich in tough connective tissue, as indicated in Figure 1Ai.b.Enzymatically digest the liver tissue with collagenase I.i.Transfer the diced liver to a sterile glass beaker and add 20 mL of sterile PBS (Figure 1Aiii).ii.Add 5 mL of collagenase I (10 mg/mL in PBS) to the liver/PBS mixture, cover with foil and incubate at 37°C in an orbital shaker with constant agitation for 30–45 min.Note: We generally incubate normal liver with collagenase I for 30 min, but more cirrhotic tissues will require up to 45 min.iii.Strain the liver homogenate through a sterile beaker lined with fine mesh (Figure 1Aiv) to remove undigested tissue and debris.2.Wash homogenate in PBS several times.a.Make volume of digest up to 200 mL with sterile PBS.b.Distribute the digest between 8 universal tubes, topping up with PBS as necessary.c.Centrifuge at 850 × g for 5 min at 21°C–23°C.d.Tip off the supernatant and resuspend the 8 pellets into 4 sterile universal containers (Figure 1Bii), washing out unused containers with PBS to ensure maximal retention of cells.Note: The pellets will be loose at this stage; therefore, care should be taken when discarding the supernatants to avoid unintentional loss of cells.e.Make up the volume to 25 mL with sterile PBS and centrifuge at 850 × g for 5 min at 21°C–23°C.f.Tip off supernatant and resuspend the 4 pellets into 2 sterile universal containers (Figure 1Biii), washing out unused containers with sterile PBS to again ensure maximal retention of cells.g.Make up the volume to 25 mL with PBS and centrifuge at 850 × g for 5 min at 21°C–23°C.h.Tip off supernatant and combine the pellets into once universal container and make up the volume with PBS to 24 mL.3.Density gradient centrifugation to isolate non-parenchymal cells.a.Add 3 mL of 33% Percoll to 8 × 15 mL centrifuge tubes.b.Carefully layer 3 mL of 77% Percoll underneath the 33% solution.Note: Be careful not to mix the two solutions too much when layering the 77% Percoll underneath the 33% solution, as this will disrupt the density gradient. A distinct interface between the two layers should be apparent when holding the tube up to a light source.c.Carefully add 3 mL of liver homogenate on top of each of the 8 Percoll gradient tubes (Figure 1Ci).d.Centrifuge at 850 × g for 25 min at 21°C–23°C, brake 0.Note: Set the brake to 0 when utilizing density gradients to ensure that the gradient is maintained, and interphase is not disturbed as the centrifuge slows.e.Remove and discard the top layer (around the 6 mL mark).f.Collect the band of cells at the interphase of the Percoll gradients (around the 3 mL mark; Figure 1Cii) and combine 2 aliquots into 1 universal container (4 universals in total; Figure 1Ciii).g.Make the volume up to 25 mL with sterile PBS and mix well to prevent the formation of another gradient.h.Centrifuge at 850 × g for 5 min at 21°C–23°C.i.Remove supernatant and combine 2 pellets into 1 universal container (2 universals in total; Figure 1Civ). Make volume up to 25 mL with sterile PBS and centrifuge at 850 × g for 5 min.j.Tip off supernatant and combine pellet into a 15 mL centrifuge tube. Make the volume up to 14 mL with sterile PBS and centrifuge at 850 × g for 5 min at 21°C–23°C.4.Depleting biliary epithelial cells (BEC) (Figure 1Di) and immune cells (Figure 1Dii).a.Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL of sterile PBS.b.Add 50 μL EpCAM antibody and incubate at 37°C for 30 min in an orbital shaker to provide constant agitation.Note: During this 30 min incubation period, put 50 mL of sterile PBS on ice in preparation for the following steps.c.Make the volume up to ∼10 mL with sterile room temperature (21°C–23°C) PBS, mix well and centrifuge at 850 × g for 5 min at 21°C–23°C.d.Tip off supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 500 μL ice-cold sterile PBS.e.Add 10 μL Goat Anti-Mouse IgG Dynabeads and 50 μL CD45 Dynabeads (ensuring that the beads are thoroughly resuspended prior to addition).f.Mix well and incubate for 30 min on ice with constant agitation.Note: An orbital shaker or benchtop rocker can be used for this purpose.g.Make up the volume to ∼6 mL with ice-cold PBS and mix well.h.Loosen lid of centrifuge tube and place in DynaMag-15 Separation Magnet for 2 min.i.With the 15 mL centrifuge tube in the magnet pipette off the supernatant and transfer to a second 15 mL centrifuge tube (do not discard).j.Place the second tube back in the magnet for 2 min and pipette off supernatant enriched for endothelial cells into a new sterile 15 mL centrifuge tube.k.Make the volume of endothelial-enriched supernatant up to 14 mL with ice-cold PBS and centrifuge 850 × g for 5 min at 4°C.5.Positive selection of endothelial cells (Figure 1Diii).a.Discard supernatant and resuspend pellet in 500 μL ice-cold PBS.b.Add 10 μL fully re-suspended CD31 Dynabeads and incubate at on ice for 30 min with constant agitation.Note: An orbital shaker or benchtop rocker can be used for this purpose.c.Make up the volume to ∼6 mL with ice-cold PBS and mix well.d.Loosen lid of centrifuge tube and place in DynaMag-15 Separation Magnet for 2 min.e.With the 15 mL centrifuge tube in the magnet pipette off the supernatant and discard.f.Remove tube from the magnet and resuspend bead-bound cells in 5 mL of complete liver endothelial medium.6.Seeding tissue culture flask.a.Transfer cell suspension into a rat tail collagen (RTC)-coated T25 culture flask.b.Place in a humidified incubator at 37°C with a 5% CO2 atmosphere.c.After 24 h replace the medium and return to incubator.Note: The yield of liver endothelial cells is highly variable and tissue dependent. Purity of isolation can be determined by immunocytochemical staining or flow cytometry. Phenotype can be determined by immunocytochemical staining and functionality can be confirmed by assays such as endocytic uptake.6Figure 1Isolation of primary liver endothelial cells from fresh human liver tissue (a diseased sample is shown)(A) (i) Liver slices from donor or diseased explants are (ii) mechanically chopped and (iii) enzymatically digested and (iv) strained through a fine mesh. (i) White arrow indicates a vascular area rich in connective tissue.(B) The digest is concentrated through a series of centrifugation steps to remove debris.(C) The digest is layered on top of a 33:77% Percoll gradient and (ii) the non-parenchymal cell fraction (white arrow) is isolated by density centrifugation. (iii and iv) Non-parenchymal cells are washed with phosphate buffered saline by centrifugation.(D) Biliary epithelial cells (BEC) and immune cells are removed by immunomagnetic selection against (i) epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM) and (ii) CD45, respectively. (iii) Liver endothelial cells are then isolated by positive immunomagnetic selection for CD31.(E) Cells are placed in culture in the presence of vascular endothelial growth factor and hepatocyte growth factor and passaged up to a maximum of five passages (p5). Scale bar represents 400 μm.

steps.title: Prepare reagents
steps.instruction: Reconstitute and aliquot all reagents needed for the workflow, following the concentrations and storage conditions described.

substeps.instruction: Reconstitute Collagenase I in sterile PBS to 10 mg/mL; aliquot and store at –20 °C for up to 1 year.
Prepare liver endothelial cell medium as listed in the key resources table.

Make Percoll stock solution: mix 99 mL Percoll with 11 mL 10× PBS. From this stock prepare a 33 % Percoll dilution (33 mL Percoll + 67 mL 1× PBS) and a 77 % Percoll dilution (77 mL Percoll + 23 mL 1× PBS). Store all Percoll solutions at 2–8 °C for up to 6 months.
Reconstitute Fixable Viability Stain 620 LIVE/DEAD: add 230 µL cell‑culture‑grade DMSO, vortex, and store at –20 °C for up to 1 year.
Prepare MACS buffer according to the composition in the key resources table.

steps.title: Prepare equipment
steps.instruction: Turn on and set up all equipment required for the isolation procedures.

substeps.instruction: Switch on the Class II microbiological safety cabinet.
Pre‑heat the orbital shaker to 37 °C.
Power on the BD Bioscience LSRFortessa X‑20 and configure lasers (488 nm, 640 nm, 405 nm, 561 nm, 355 nm).
Coat T25 and T75 tissue‑culture flasks with rat‑tail collagen as described in the materials section.

steps.title: Digest liver tissue
steps.instruction: Generate a single‑cell suspension from fresh human liver tissue.

substeps.instruction: Mechanically chop ~75 g of liver tissue with sterile scalpels in a 150 × 20 mm petri dish until a coarse paste is obtained; excise highly vascular regions beforehand.

Transfer the diced tissue to a sterile glass beaker, add 20 mL sterile PBS, then add 5 mL Collagenase I (10 mg/mL in PBS). Cover with foil and incubate on the 37 °C orbital shaker with constant agitation for 30 min (up to 45 min for cirrhotic tissue).
Strain the homogenate through a sterile beaker lined with fine mesh to remove undigested fragments.

steps.title: Wash homogenate
steps.instruction: Remove debris and concentrate cells by repeated PBS washes and centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Adjust the digest volume to 200 mL with sterile PBS.
Distribute the digest into eight universal tubes, topping up with PBS as needed.
Centrifuge each tube at 850 × g for 5 min at 21–23 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the eight pellets in four sterile universal containers (wash unused containers with PBS to retain cells).
Bring each suspension to 25 mL with sterile PBS, centrifuge again at 850 × g for 5 min at 21–23 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the four pellets in two sterile universal containers, bring to 25 mL with PBS, centrifuge a third time under the same conditions.
Combine all pellets into one universal container and adjust the final volume to 24 mL with PBS.

steps.title: Density gradient centrifugation
steps.instruction: Separate non‑parenchymal cells using a Percoll step gradient.

substeps.instruction: In eight 15 mL centrifuge tubes add 3 mL of 33 % Percoll.
Carefully layer 3 mL of 77 % Percoll underneath each 33 % layer without mixing.
Gently add 3 mL of the liver homogenate on top of each gradient.
Centrifuge at 850 × g for 25 min at 21–23 °C with brake set to 0.
Discard the top ~6 mL layer.
Collect the interphase band (~3 mL) from each tube; combine two aliquots into one universal container (four containers total).
Bring the combined interphase to 25 mL with sterile PBS, mix well, then centrifuge at 850 × g for 5 min at 21–23 °C.
Discard supernatant, combine the two resulting pellets into one container, bring to 25 mL with PBS, and centrifuge again at 850 × g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant, combine the final pellet into a 15 mL tube, bring to 14 mL with PBS, and centrifuge at 850 × g for 5 min at 21–23 °C.

steps.title: Deplete BEC and immune cells
steps.instruction: Remove biliary epithelial cells and CD45⁺ immune cells by immunomagnetic negative selection.

substeps.instruction: Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 500 µL sterile PBS.
Add 50 µL EpCAM antibody, incubate at 37 °C for 30 min on the orbital shaker.
While incubating, place 50 mL sterile PBS on ice for later use.
Adjust the volume to ~10 mL with room‑temperature PBS (21–23 °C), mix, and centrifuge at 850 × g for 5 min at 21–23 °C.
Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 500 µL ice‑cold PBS.
Add 10 µL Goat Anti‑Mouse IgG Dynabeads and 50 µL CD45 Dynabeads (beads must be fully resuspended).
Mix and incubate on ice for 30 min with constant agitation.
Bring the suspension to ~6 mL with ice‑cold PBS, mix well.
Place the tube in a DynaMag‑15 magnet for 2 min, then pipette off the supernatant into a second 15 mL tube (do not discard).
Return the second tube to the magnet for another 2 min and transfer the supernatant (enriched for endothelial cells) to a new sterile 15 mL tube.
Adjust the endothelial‑enriched supernatant to 14 mL with ice‑cold PBS and centrifuge at 850 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Positive selection of endothelial cells
steps.instruction: Capture CD31⁺ liver endothelial cells with magnetic beads.

substeps.instruction: Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 500 µL ice‑cold PBS.
Add 10 µL fully resuspended CD31 Dynabeads, incubate on ice for 30 min with constant agitation.
Bring the volume to ~6 mL with ice‑cold PBS and mix.
Place the tube in the DynaMag‑15 magnet for 2 min.
While in the magnet, pipette off the supernatant and discard it.
Remove the tube from the magnet and resuspend the bead‑bound endothelial cells in 5 mL complete liver endothelial cell medium.

steps.title: Seed endothelial cells
steps.instruction: Plate the isolated endothelial cells and expand them in culture.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the 5 mL cell suspension into a rat‑tail‑collagen‑coated T25 flask.
Place the flask in a humidified incubator at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂.
After 24 h replace the medium with fresh liver endothelial cell medium and return the flask to the incubator.

steps.title: Isolate monocytes – density gradient
steps.instruction: Obtain peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from whole blood using Lympholyte‑H.

substeps.instruction: Add 15 mL Lympholyte‑H Cell Separation Media to a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Carefully layer 20–30 mL whole blood (collected in EDTA tubes) on top of the Lympholyte‑H.
Centrifuge at 850 × g for 20 min at 21–23 °C with no brake.

steps.title: Isolate PBMC layer
steps.instruction: Collect and wash the buffy coat containing PBMCs.

substeps.instruction: Remove the buffy‑coat layer and transfer it to a sterile 50 mL tube.
Adjust the volume to 40 mL with sterile PBS and centrifuge at 850 × g for 5 min at 21–23 °C.
Discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 40 mL sterile PBS, then centrifuge at 350 × g for 10 min at 21–23 °C to remove platelets.
Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 20 mL sterile PBS.
Pass the PBMC suspension through a 70 µm cell strainer to obtain a single‑cell suspension.
Keep all solutions on ice and work quickly to avoid monocyte activation.

steps.title: Magnetic labeling of PBMCs
steps.instruction: Label PBMCs with the Pan Monocyte Isolation Kit reagents for negative selection.

substeps.instruction: Count total PBMCs using a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the PBMC suspension at 850 × g for 5 min at 21–23 °C and discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 30 µL MACS buffer per 10⁷ PBMCs.
Add 10 µL FcR Blocking Reagent per 10⁷ PBMCs and mix.
Add 10 µL Biotin‑Antibody Cocktail per 10⁷ PBMCs and mix.
Incubate 5 min on ice with constant agitation.
Add 30 µL kit‑provided buffer per 10⁷ cells and mix.
Add 20 µL Anti‑Biotin MicroBeads per 10⁷ cells and mix.
Incubate 10 min on ice with constant agitation.

steps.title: Magnetic separation of monocytes
steps.instruction: Perform negative selection of CD14⁺ monocytes using LS columns.

substeps.instruction: Place an LS Separation column in the magnetic field of a MidiMACS separator.
Rinse the column with 3 mL MACS buffer, allowing the flow‑through to collect in a 15 mL tube (wait until the column reservoir is empty).
Apply the labeled PBMC suspension to the column; collect the flow‑through (enriched CD14⁺ monocytes) in a new sterile 15 mL tube.
Wash the column with an additional 3 mL MACS buffer, collecting this wash in the same tube.
If desired, repeat the column loading and washing steps to increase purity.

steps.title: Resuspend monocytes for assay
steps.instruction: Count monocytes and keep them on ice in shear‑flow assay buffer.

substeps.instruction: Determine the total number of isolated monocytes with a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the monocyte suspension at 850 × g for 5 min and discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in Endothelial SFM + 0.1 % BSA at 1 mL per 10⁶ monocytes.
Keep the monocyte suspension on ice until the shear‑flow assay is performed.

steps.title: Pre‑label endothelial cells
steps.instruction: Stain cultured liver endothelial monolayers with fluorescent dyes before the flow assay.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the confluent endothelial layer with CellTracker Green and SiR‑actin in shear‑flow assay medium for 30 min at 37 °C.
Wash briefly with assay medium before adding monocytes.

steps.title: Fix and stain for transmigration analysis
steps.instruction: Fix cells after the flow assay and perform immunofluorescent staining to identify transmigration routes.

substeps.instruction: Fix the cells with 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) (duration as per standard protocol).
Stain nuclei with DAPI, endothelial junctions with anti‑VE‑cadherin antibody, and retain CellTracker Green and SiR‑actin signals.

Acquire confocal images; identify monocytes (DAPI‑positive, smaller nuclei) and assess VE‑cadherin continuity to distinguish paracellular (VE‑cadherin break) from transcellular (F‑actin enrichment around the cell) migration.
